summary: @servicetitan/marketing-global-route ships install-time Bun-runtime dropper executing obfuscated payload
details: The package's preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts it to a temporary directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file math_init.js shipped in the tarball. math_init.js is a ~727 KB heavily obfuscated Bun-CJS bundle (string-array rotation via a WV8StW rotator, hex-mangled _0x identifiers, thousands of numeric/string constants) that is not referenced by the declared main entry dist/index.js. The package's stated purpose is a small MobX/React route-mapping TypeScript helper published under the @servicetitan scope, which has no relation to a Bun-executed obfuscated bundle named math_init.js. The alternate-runtime execution pattern is used so that a Node-based scanner cannot statically evaluate the payload. Package metadata is thin (empty author field) despite the vendor-scoped name, consistent with a scope-hijack shape. On npm install, arbitrary Bun-interpreted code from the shipped obfuscated bundle runs on the installer's machine before any user code is invoked.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
